Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator (QEMU functional + vsim cycle-accurate, two-phase handoff QEMU1 -> vsim).
CANONICAL docs that are the source of truth and MUST be kept (do not recommend deleting these): CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md (always-current user guide), docs/FRS.md, docs/MRD.md, ROADMAP.md (master FR tracker, "single source of truth"), driver/ROADMAP.md (C++ andes-sim driver tracker), docs/engine_interface.md, docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb (the L-id capability-gap envelope).
The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `vscratch_reservation.md`

Steps:
1. Read `vscratch_reservation.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

1	# V-scratch reservation: move the transport page out of the program's RAM
2	
3	## Problem (L26)
4	
5	The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
6	window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
7	That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
8	data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
9	corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
10	`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.
11	
12	## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)
13	
14	Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
15	physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
16	`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
17	in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
18	without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
19	detected after the fact.
20	
21	```
22	            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
23	V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
24	            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
25	            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
26	            +----------------+ ram_base
27	```
28	
29	Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
30	mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
31	value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
32	"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
33	lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.
34	
35	Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
36	Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
37	"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.
38	
39	## Features
40	
41	### F1. Runtime scratch GPA = top page of the mmap span  [state: DONE]
42	- Verified 2026-06-15: host unit suites green -- v_regfile_xfer 3/3,
43	  resume_driver 33/33, state_drain 32/32 (incl. new unset-guard tests), +18
44	  other hybrid suites. vsim builds all 5 CPUs. Full marker e2e 22/22 (incl. V
45	  fixtures + S/U ax66). `break_vscratch.elf` (the L26 repro) now PASSES under
46	  `--model hybrid --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (was a hang) -- the 0x00FF0000
47	  sentinel survives because the V transport relocated to the mmap top page.
48	- Design note: `scratch_gpa` is a required-when-V ctor arg on ResumeDriver /
49	  StateDrain, defaulting to a `kVScratchGpaUnset` sentinel; a V handoff that
50	  reaches the sweep unset throws (no silent transport via a bogus address).
51	  The 60+ non-V unit-test ctor sites pass a stand-in (kScratch); the real glue
52	  (simulator.hpp `v_scratch_gpa()`) threads the live value through the two
53	  controllers.
54	- NOT yet run as e2e: cosim / lockstep V paths (their drain_full /
55	  drain_checkpoint scratch logic is covered at unit level; same threading).
56	- Replace the fixed `kVScratchGpa` constant with `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
57	  ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`. The scratch is the top
58	  `kVScratchBytes` of whatever RAM span is mapped.
59	- Host stager (`stage_v_to_scratch` / `read_v_from_scratch`) computes the
60	  offset as `ram_size - kVScratchBytes` (it already receives the span + base).
61	- `ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` take the scratch GPA as a required ctor arg
62	  (no silent default) and pass it to `pb_v_data_sweep`.
63	- `simulator.hpp` construction sites compute the GPA from
64	  `platform.main_memory` and pass it down.
65	- After F1 alone the scratch is the top page of `mem_size` (scheme A: inside
66	  program RAM, but far above this runtime's 7 MB stack -- already better than
67	  the mid-RAM 15 MB constant). F2 lifts it above program RAM (scheme D).
68	- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `resume_driver.hpp`,
69	  `state_drain.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp` (caller), `simulator.hpp`,
70	  `resume_from_qemu.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`, `lockstep_controller.hpp`;
71	  tests `tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
72	  `state_drain.test.cpp`.
73	- Deps: none.
74	
75	### F2. Map one page above --mem-size; scratch sits above program RAM  [state: DONE]
76	- Verified 2026-06-16: shared ABI gained `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`
77	  (= 32*HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX); v_regfile_xfer's `kVScratchBytes` references it.
78	  Driver helpers `physical_mmap_bytes()` / `max_program_mem_bytes()` (shm.cpp,
79	  unit-tested in infra-test); `run_plan.cpp` allocates + reports the physical
80	  size (program + page); `cmd_run.cpp` caps --mem-size at 2G - page;
81	  `tests/e2e.sh` mmap split into PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES.
82	- Proof: driver builds; 9 driver unit suites + plan-itest pass; V e2e 4/4 with
83	  the larger mmap. NEW guard `tests/fixtures/break_vscratch_top.S` writes a
84	  sentinel at the program's LAST page (0x07FFF000 @128M) and PASSES under
85	  hybrid -- the sentinel survives the V transport, proving the scratch moved to
86	  the ceiling (0x08000000), above program RAM. Under F1/scheme A that page WAS
87	  the scratch and the fixture would hang.
88	- Note: only the hybrid (shared-mmap) path reserves the page; `--model fast`
89	  (plain `-m`, no handoff, no scratch) is untouched.
90	- Driver: physical mmap / QEMU backend size / vsim `--shared-mem-size` =
91	  `mem_size + kVScratchBytes`; the program's RAM ceiling stays `mem_size`.
92	- 2 GiB edge: `mem_size + 4 KB` would cross into MROM at 0x80000000, so cap
93	  usable `--mem-size` at `2G - 4 KB` (doc note; 2G was always approximate, L7).
94	- `tests/e2e.sh` shared-mmap setup must add the page too (it sizes its own
95	  mmap for the e2e path).
96	- Key files: `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/shm.cpp`, `driver/plan.*`,
97	  `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `tests/e2e.sh`; driver unit tests.
98	- Deps: F1.
99	
100	### F3. Load-time overlap check (loud abort)  [state: DONE]
101	- Verified 2026-06-16: `elf_load_top()` (elf_syms.cpp) returns the highest
102	  PT_LOAD `p_paddr + p_memsz`; `cmd_run.cpp` rejects a hybrid run when that
103	  exceeds the scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size). Unit: elf-syms test
104	  (load-top on a fixture + non-ELF err) + 9/9 driver suites. Integration:
105	  `--mem-size 1M` on a fixture linked at 0x100000 aborts with "ELF static image
106	  ends at 0x100036, overlapping the reserved V-transport scratch page at
107	  0x100000 ... raise --mem-size"; default 128M runs clean (no false positive).
108	- Scope: static image only (PT_LOAD). Runtime heap/stack growth into the
109	  scratch is already impossible under F2 (scratch is above the program ceiling).
110	- Reject any ELF segment (and ideally the initial SP) overlapping
111	  `[scratch_gpa, scratch_gpa + kVScratchBytes)`. With F2 this never fires for
112	  well-behaved programs; it converts the paranoid "program pokes past its own
113	  ceiling" case from silent corruption into a clear error.
114	- Key files: driver ELF loader / vsim `state_loader.hpp`; new unit test.
115	- Deps: F1, F2.
116	
117	### F4. Docs  [state: DONE]
118	- Done 2026-06-16: `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb` L26 -> RESOLVED (scheme D
119	  fix narrative) + quick-ref row; L10 updated (scratch GPA is now runtime-
120	  derived, no longer a porting blocker). `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` 2.5 (--mem-size is
121	  program RAM; driver maps +1 page for the scratch; cap 2G-page; ELF-overlap
122	  reject). `CLAUDE.md` V-State Transport (top-page GPA, required-when-V arg,
123	  +1-page mmap). `runtime/andes-sim.ld` comment (no fixed reservation).
124	- ABI DRY: `v_regfile_xfer.hpp` `kVScratchBytes` now references the shared
125	  `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`; host units + vsim rebuilt green.
126	- `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md` (a draft gem5/virt-parity design
127	  archive that still cited a fixed `kVScratchGpa = 0x80FF0000`) was removed
128	  2026-06-16 at the user's request.
129	- Deps: F1, F2, F3.

538:   "source": "## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker. The retired Python golden
  (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`) keeps its own hardcoded copies.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`,
    orchestrator `abi.py`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andes-sim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andes-sim run --model fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--model hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andes_sim/roi.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:663-671` (marker matcher);
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:663-671`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary (`hsim.py:1126-1225`,
  `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at
     each window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without
     warmup the CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate
     inherits SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py:1126-1225` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). Note: SimPoint
  still runs only on the Python golden (`./hsim.py`); the C++ port has not
  landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3, see `vscratch_reservation.md`)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."

375	### 2.5 Requesting memory (`--mem-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)
376	
377	By default every `./andes-sim` (and `./hsim.py`) invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
378	a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
379	workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
380	RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:
381	
382	| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
383	|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
384	| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias, also on `profile`, `archive`, `estimate`) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |
385	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | pin the backing directory (skips the tier list below). |
386	
387	Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:
388	
389	| Model    | What it does |
390	|----------|--------------|
391	| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). The driver maps one extra 4 KiB page on top for the V-register transport scratch (L26): the physical shared mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window = `--mem-size + 4 KiB`, with the scratch parked in that top page, just above everything your program can address. You get your full `--mem-size`; the page is invisible. The driver rejects `> 2G - 4 KiB` **before** allocating, and rejects an ELF whose static image would extend into the reserved page (`raise --mem-size`). |
392	| `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. QEMU itself rejects `> 2G`. |
393	| `cycle`  | validate-only: the cycle engine always models its full DRAM window, so there is nothing to size (the driver says so on stderr). |
394	
395	Backing-directory selection (`./andes-sim`): a two-tier list, first fit
396	wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):
397	
398	1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
399	2. `~/.cache/andes-sim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the
400	   size ceiling becomes disk free space. Hot pages still sit in the
401	   kernel page cache, so the cost vs tmpfs is background writeback only.
402	
403	We never switch **silently**: the status line always names the chosen
404	dir, and a fallback adds the reason, e.g.
405	`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andes-sim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))`.
406	`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single dir with **no** fallback past it: rc=2
407	with a hint if it can't hold the request. (The retired `./hsim.py`
408	golden keeps the old pin-or-/dev/shm rule with no tier list.)
409	
410	Examples:
411	
412	```sh
413	# Small request; /dev/shm fits, so tier 1 is chosen.
414	./andes-sim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 256M
415	#   [hsim mmap] 256.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 252.0 GiB)
416	
417	# 2 GiB request on a small-RAM box: falls through to the disk tier,
418	# and the status line says so.
419	./andes-sim run my.elf --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2G
420	#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andes-sim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
421	
422	# Pin a scratch filesystem instead (no fallback past the pin):
423	HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch/hsim \
424	  ./andes-sim run my.elf --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2G

The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

+
+## Problem (L26)
+
+The V-register transport stages 32 vector registers through a 4 KB guest-RAM
+window at the **compile-time constant** `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MB).
+That address sits *inside* the program's usable RAM, so a program that places
+data there (large heap, custom linker script, direct addressing) is silently
+corrupted on every resume -- even if it never uses V. Demonstrated by
+`tests/fixtures/break_vscratch.S`.
+
+## Core architecture (the fix: scheme D)
+
+Put the scratch page **just above the program's declared RAM**, by making the
+physical mmap one page larger than `--mem-size`. The program is told it has
+`mem_size`; the simulator quietly maps `mem_size + 4 KB` and parks the scratch
+in the extra page. No program layout can reach a page above its own ceiling
+without a bug, so the collision class is removed at the root rather than
+detected after the fact.
+
+```
+            +----------------+ ram_base + mmap_size            (physical top)
+V scratch ->|  V scratch 4KB |   mmap_size = mem_size + 4 KB
+            +----------------+ ram_base + mem_size             (program ceiling)
+            |  program RAM   |   text / data / heap / stack -- all strictly below
+            +----------------+ ram_base
+```
+
+Scratch GPA = `ram_base + mmap_size - kVScratchBytes` = the **top page of the
+mmap**. Both legs already receive `mmap_size`, so the address stays a derived
+value with **no new field to keep in sync** -- the only change vs the naive
+"top of RAM" is that the mmap is one page bigger than the program's RAM, which
+lifts the scratch above everything the program can legally address.
+
+Invariant that must hold at every step: **the host stager and the vsim
+Program-Buffer sweep must use the SAME scratch address.** That is why the
+"runtime GPA" work (F1) lands as one atomic unit across all three users.
+
+## Features
+
+### F1. Runtime scratch GPA = top page of the mmap span  [state: DONE]
+- Verified 2026-06-15: host unit suites green -- v_regfile_xfer 3/3,
+  resume_driver 33/33, state_drain 32/32 (incl. new unset-guard tests), +18
+  other hybrid suites. vsim builds all 5 CPUs. Full marker e2e 22/22 (incl. V
+  fixtures + S/U ax66). `break_vscratch.elf` (the L26 repro) now PASSES under
+  `--model hybrid --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (was a hang) -- the 0x00FF0000
+  sentinel survives because the V transport relocated to the mmap top page.
+- Design note: `scratch_gpa` is a required-when-V ctor arg on ResumeDriver /
+  StateDrain, defaulting to a `kVScratchGpaUnset` sentinel; a V handoff that
+  reaches the sweep unset throws (no silent transport via a bogus address).
+  The 60+ non-V unit-test ctor sites pass a stand-in (kScratch); the real glue
+  (simulator.hpp `v_scratch_gpa()`) threads the live value through the two
+  controllers.
+- NOT yet run as e2e: cosim / lockstep V paths (their drain_full /
+  drain_checkpoint scratch logic is covered at unit level; same threading).
+- Replace the fixed `kVScratchGpa` constant with `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
+  ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`. The scratch is the top
+  `kVScratchBytes` of whatever RAM span is mapped.
+- Host stager (`stage_v_to_scratch` / `read_v_from_scratch`) computes the
+  offset as `ram_size - kVScratchBytes` (it already receives the span + base).
+- `ResumeDriver` / `StateDrain` take the scratch GPA as a required ctor arg
+  (no silent default) and pass it to `pb_v_data_sweep`.
+- `simulator.hpp` construction sites compute the GPA from
+  `platform.main_memory` and pass it down.
+- After F1 alone the scratch is the top page of `mem_size` (scheme A: inside
+  program RAM, but far above this runtime's 7 MB stack -- already better than
+  the mid-RAM 15 MB constant). F2 lifts it above program RAM (scheme D).
+- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `resume_driver.hpp`,
+  `state_drain.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp` (caller), `simulator.hpp`,
+  `resume_from_qemu.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`, `lockstep_controller.hpp`;
+  tests `tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
+  `state_drain.test.cpp`.
+- Deps: none.
+
+### F2. Map one page above --mem-size; scratch sits above program RAM  [state: DONE]
+- Verified 2026-06-16: shared ABI gained `HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`
+  (= 32*HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX); v_regfile_xfer's `kVScratchBytes` references it.
+  Driver helpers `physical_mmap_bytes()` / `max_program_mem_bytes()` (shm.cpp,
+  unit-tested in infra-test); `run_plan.cpp` allocates + reports the physical
+  size (program + page); `cmd_run.cpp` caps --mem-size at 2G - page;
+  `tests/e2e.sh` mmap split into PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES.
+- Proof: driver builds; 9 driver unit suites + plan-itest pass; V e2e 4/4 with
+  the larger mmap. NEW guard `tests/fixtures/break_vscratch_top.S` writes a
+  sentinel at the program's LAST page (0x07FFF000 @128M) and PASSES under
+  hybrid -- the sentinel survives the V transport, proving the scratch moved to
+  the ceiling (0x08000000), above program RAM. Under F1/scheme A that page WAS
+  the scratch and the fixture would hang.
+- Note: only the hybrid (shared-mmap) path reserves the page; `--model fast`
+  (plain `-m`, no handoff, no scratch) is untouched.
+- Driver: physical mmap / QEMU backend size / vsim `--shared-mem-size` =
+  `mem_size + kVScratchBytes`; the program's RAM ceiling stays `mem_size`.
+- 2 GiB edge: `mem_size + 4 KB` would cross into MROM at 0x80000000, so cap
+  usable `--mem-size` at `2G - 4 KB` (doc note; 2G was always approximate, L7).
+- `tests/e2e.sh` shared-mmap setup must add the page too (it sizes its own
+  mmap for the e2e path).
+- Key files: `driver/cmd_run.cpp`, `driver/shm.cpp`, `driver/plan.*`,
+  `driver/engine_registry.cpp`, `tests/e2e.sh`; driver unit tests.
+- Deps: F1.
+
+### F3. Load-time overlap check (loud abort)  [state: DONE]
+- Verified 2026-06-16: `elf_load_top()` (elf_syms.cpp) returns the highest
+  PT_LOAD `p_paddr + p_memsz`; `cmd_run.cpp` rejects a hybrid run when that
+  exceeds the scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size). Unit: elf-syms test
+  (load-top on a fixture + non-ELF err) + 9/9 driver suites. Integration:
+  `--mem-size 1M` on a fixture linked at 0x100000 aborts with "ELF static image
+  ends at 0x100036, overlapping the reserved V-transport scratch page at
+  0x100000 ... raise --mem-size"; default 128M runs clean (no false positive).
+- Scope: static image only (PT_LOAD). Runtime heap/stack growth into the
+  scratch is already impossible under F2 (scratch is above the program ceiling).
+- Reject any ELF segment (and ideally the initial SP) overlapping
+  `[scratch_gpa, scratch_gpa + kVScratchBytes)`. With F2 this never fires for
+  well-behaved programs; it converts the paranoid "program pokes past its own
+  ceiling" case from silent corruption into a clear error.
+- Key files: driver ELF loader / vsim `state_loader.hpp`; new unit test.
+- Deps: F1, F2.
+
+### F4. Docs  [state: DONE]
